front: Probability of event A (equally likely outcomes)?

back: Trial: one repetition of an experiment. Outcome: a possible result. Sample space $U$: the set of all outcomes. Event: a set of outcomes.
$\dfrac{\text{number of times the event occurs}}{\text{number of trials}}$ — an experimental estimate of $P(A)$, improving with more trials.

front: A fair die is rolled 120 times. Expected number of sixes?
P(at least one six in 4 rolls of a fair die)?

back: Sample space has 36 equally likely outcomes, 6 give 7: $\frac6{36} = \frac16$.

front: "Sum of two dice is 2 to 12, so P(sum = 7) $= \frac1{11}$." Error?
back: $\frac{n(A)}{n(U)}$ needs equally likely outcomes; the 11 sums are not. Use the 36 ordered pairs.
